md_docs_2client-connection-lifecycle(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2client-connection-lifecycle(3)

NAME

md_docs_2client-connection-lifecycle - Shared connection ownership

src/client/connection.c owns one native connection attempt, including dialing, handshake state, transport/client handle, worker pool, outbound audio queue, video encoder, audio pipeline, and protocol/snapshot state. Each retry allocates a fresh owner. Capture devices, media sources, terminal UI, and reconnect policy belong to the application and may outlive an attempt. WebSocket clients also retain one application runtime context: libwebsockets 4.5 tears down process TLS when its last context is destroyed, so an application reference keeps TLS alive across retries. It is released after the final connection and application media cleanup. See the upstream TLS destructor.

Startup moves from STARTING to RUNNING. Acquisition failures, peer disconnects, and application shutdown all leave through client_connection_destroy(). Startup records initialized synchronization objects separately from workers so partial queue initialization also unwinds. No "all workers started" flag gates cleanup.

The reusable state machine lives in src/common/session/connection.c. It owns startup/stop state and the controlling-thread boundary, and enforces interruption, joining, then release. Mode adapters supply resource-specific operations. Native client attempts, discovery participants, and discovery WebRTC media workers all use that sequence. Discovery still coordinates signaling, host control, media transport switching, and host migration.

Workers, ACIP callbacks, and crypto negotiation receive their connection context explicitly. There is no current-connection singleton or thread-local replacement. Each attempt holds its own crypto callbacks and user data. Multiple owners can coexist on one thread or in one program. Application media devices, capture, and display are borrowed explicitly; applications must provide distinct resources when running independent media sessions. The CLI still runs one interactive session. Signal handlers publish exit/resize requests without walking owners.

Shutdown publishes STOPPING, interrupts network I/O without taking the send mutex, and wakes the audio sender before joining workers. Worker join failure retains the owner and all dependencies; the controlling thread keeps waiting before allowing application cleanup or reconnect. Queue synchronization, encoders, audio pipeline, and crypto state are released only after their users stop. The embedded connection handle remains the sole transport/client owner throughout startup and teardown.

The audio device context persists, but its pipeline and buffered samples are reset for each connection. Snapshot teardown interrupts I/O before joining capture. The former encoder flush allocated and logged buffered output without transmitting it; teardown no longer runs that operation concurrently with capture.

Validation

Build with the default Debug preset and run:

uv run --project tests/ascii_chat_tests --frozen python -m pytest tests/python/integration/client_connection --ascii-chat-binary build/bin/ascii-chat
uv run --project tests/ascii_chat_tests --frozen python -m pytest tests/python/integration/network/test_server_client_lifecycle.py --ascii-chat-binary build/bin/ascii-chat
uv run --project tests/ascii_chat_tests --frozen python -m pytest tests/python/integration/network --ascii-chat-binary build/bin/ascii-chat

Use ascii-chat.exe on Windows. The new suite also registers as the Debug CTest client-connection-lifecycle. It injects failures after 13 acquisition stages, repeats partial-startup failures in one process, reconnects one live client three times over both TCP and WebSocket, and races abrupt peer loss with local interrupt. It verifies each attempt releases its workers and a fresh attempt starts with empty protocol state. These cases use test video and software test audio with playback disabled, exercising the audio pipeline, capture, and sender without webcam or audio hardware.

ASCII_CHAT_TEST_CLIENT_FAIL_STAGE selects an acquisition checkpoint in Debug builds only. It has no effect in release builds.

The Criterion-free session-connections test runs two live TCP owners with blocked receive workers, stops one while checking that the other keeps receiving, injects a failed join, checks controlling-thread cleanup, and unwinds partial startup. participant-media exercises discovery participant failures, repeated media lifecycles, transport transfer, recovery, and host-control preservation. discovery-session-process covers production discovery state transitions. Discovery media teardown also retains its stack dependencies until worker joins succeed; NAT-worker join failures retain the discovery session for a safe retry.
